results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: Nebius GPU Price Hike: H100 to B300 Cloud Prices Rise | metir Blog
results.author: Metir AI Team
highlights:
On October 1, 2026, the Nebius GPU price hike took effect: the neocloud raised on-demand rates for Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 instances by roughly 17% to 21%. Nebius's own pricing page now lists the new rates with that effective date and notes that prices exclude taxes and may change at any time (Nebius pricing). It is the second increase in a few months, and it runs against the story most people remember from 2024 and 2025, when GPU rental prices mostly fell.

$3.85 to $4.50 H100 per GPU-hour (+17%)

$4.50 to $5.40 H200 per GPU-hour (+20%)

$7.15 to $8.50 B200 per GPU-hour (+19%)

$7.85 to $9.50 B300 per GPU-hour (+21%)

NVIDIA

The hike covers Nvidia GPU instances and AMD EPYC Genoa CPU capacity.

## What changed in the Nebius GPU price hike

Nebius's pricing page lists these on-demand rates per GPU-hour, before and from October 1: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, H200 $4.50 to $5.40, B200 $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 $7.85 to $9.50 (Nebius pricing). Our arithmetic on those figures gives 16.9%, 20.0%, 18.9% and 21.0%, matching press coverage.

Early coverage disagreed about sourcing. Stocktwits said the details came from Nebius's communication to customers, reshared on Reddit and X, with no official public statement in its report. results.title: Nebius removes its spot-price ceiling — preemptible GPUs can now cost more than on-demand | GPUJournal
highlights:
In an update note dated Nov 2, 2026 on its own blog, Nebius says the cap that kept its dynamic spot price one cent below the on-demand rate is gone. Spot still has a floor — it just no longer has a top, and setting your own max price is now the only brake.

...

What changed, from Nebius's own post “Introducing spot pricing for preemptible VMs” (published Sep ... 2, 2026; read Nov ... , ... 026): its update note, dated Nov ... 2026, reads — “this section ... stated that the spot price always stays between a floor and a ceiling one cent below the ... -demand rate. We have removed the ceiling. Customers can cap what they pay by setting a max price.” The post's how-it-works section now states plainly: “There is no upper limit, so during periods of high demand the spot price can rise above the on-demand GPU-hour rate.”

...

What did not change: Nebius's on-demand list. Re-read on Nebius's own prices page on Nov 2, 2026, B300 is $9.50 an hour, B200 $8.50, H200 $5.40, H100 $4.50, RTX PRO 6000 $1.80 and L40S from $1.55 — every figure the same as our Nov 1 read. This is not a price rise in the list; it is the removal of the guarantee that the interruptible lane is always the cheaper one.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

...

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

The full issue, with every provider's lowest observed price and the method notes, is here:
https://lnkd.in/efqfwQWm

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to 21%; H100 cumulative gain of 53% over five months

Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: KuCoin News

A notable shift is emerging in the AI computing power market: while cloud providers continue to expand their data centers, rental prices for certain high-end GPUs are not declining with increased supply—they continue to rise.

According to a price adjustment notice sent by Nebius to its customers, effective October 1, 2026, the company plans to increase prices for multiple on-demand GPU instances by approximately 17% to 21%. The proposed hourly rates per GPU are: H100 rising from $3.85 to $4.50 (a 16.9% increase), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase), B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (18.9% increase), and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (21% increase).

This price adjustment sends a significant signal: the pace of growth in AI computing demand may still outstrip the rate at which high-end GPUs, power, and data center capacity are coming online. Unlike traditional cloud computing, the core scarce resources for AI cloud services extend beyond servers to include GPU availability, power access, liquid cooling systems, networking equipment, and data centers capable of supporting high-density racks. If any single component encounters a bottleneck, new computing power cannot be rapidly deployed.

At the Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Nebius management stated that the company's visibility into customer demand has extended from approximately 18 months to over 24 months, with some customers already reserving compute capacity for the first half of 2028. The company previously conducted price testing for scarce Blackwell capacity, achieving transaction prices approximately 15% higher than previous peak prices and roughly 20% higher than standard sales pipeline quotes.

The significance of Nebius's price increase lies not merely in the ability to charge approximately 20% more per GPU hour, but in confirming that supply and demand in the AI computing market still favor suppliers. A primary past market concern was that simultaneous launches of numerous data centers could eventually lead to GPU leasing market oversupply, potentially resulting in lower utilization rates, extended payback periods, and asset impairment for companies built under assumptions of higher prices. Nebius signals the opposite: the company is raising prices not only for new B200 and B300 models but also for H100 and H200, which have been on the market for years. This indicates that demand extends beyond the latest architecture, with previous-generation GPUs still offering sufficient performance and cost efficiency for model fine-tuning, inference, scientific computing, and certain enterprise workloads.

...

However, the on-demand price increase will not uniformly raise all of Nebius's revenue by 20%. Large customers typically sign multi-year contracts with fixed prices, minimum purchase volumes, and service terms that cannot be immediately repriced according to new public rates. This adjustment most directly impacts on-demand and short-term compute contracts rather than long-term capacity agreements already signed by clients like Meta.
